clue.text: Waking with alarm at hand, vacant thought lapses

parts.note: something at hand is near, or nigh

indicators.note: vacant means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters of the word thought

parts.note: lapses are slips or mistakes

explanation.surface: Someone wakes in a fright, their reasoning slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties THOUGHT of its insides, leaving TT.
explanation.definitionFit: These are episodes of sudden panic-stricken waking from deep sleep, common in young children.

clue.text: Tennis as partly reviewed?

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters of the phrase are gone over again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tennis, seen again in bits on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges the fourteen letters of TENNIS AS PARTLY; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since televised tennis shows key points again.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast sport repeats key moments of play, often in slow motion, so a viewer sees part of the match a second time.

clue.text: Poet's contribution to the ineffable

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poet adds something to the indescribable.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Heine was a nineteenth-century German lyric poet; the 's here is 'is', so the poet is the one contributing.

clue.text: A new roost roughly welcomed by itinerant?

definitions.text: A new roost roughly welcomed by itinerant?

indicators.note: welcomed by says the following word takes the earlier pieces inside itself

parts.note: an itinerant is a wanderer, a tramp
to roost is to perch, or sit
C is short for circa, Latin for roughly or about

explanation.surface: A wanderer finds a fresh place to rest for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' signals the container; the whole clue also describes the answer, a temporary shelter for people on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit camp is temporary accommodation for travellers, refugees or troops passing through, roughly a new roost for a wanderer.

clue.text: One gets back into circulation when baldness is cured

definitions.text: One gets back into circulation when baldness is cured

parts.words: One gets back into circulation when baldness is cured
parts.note: reads like a man regaining his social life after a hair cure, but describes a worn tyre given a new tread so it can go back on the road

explanation.surface: A man returns to the social scene once his hair grows back.
explanation.walkthrough: A tyre worn smooth is called bald; renewing its tread puts it back into use on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A remoulded tyre has fresh tread bonded onto a worn casing, so it can be used again.

clue.text: Blemish reduced after upsetting medical procedures

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so the word is read backwards
reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the word for blemish goes

parts.note: a blemish is a spot

explanation.surface: A skin mark shrinks after some surgery upsets the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts SPOT to SPO; 'upsetting' turns that over to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ops is the everyday short form of operations, surgical procedures.

clue.text: Person lagging behind to keep out of alignment, holding both hands apart

indicators.note: apart means the two hands go in separately, at different places
holding means the word for out of alignment keeps something within it

parts.note: to stagger is to set things so they do not line up
R and L are the abbreviations for right and left, the two hands
R and L are the abbreviations for right and left, the two hands

explanation.surface: A slow walker keeps falling out of line, arms spread wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'apart' put R and L into STAGGER in two separate places: ST-R-AGG-L-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler trails behind the rest of a group, falling back from the main body.

clue.text: Feminist writer crushed swot, penning lines with a certain dexterity

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the scrambled word takes the lines inside
crushed means the letters of swot are broken up and reformed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
a certain one, as in 'a certain person', gives the word one
craft is skill or dexterity

explanation.surface: A studious type is squashed while writing with some skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' gives WOST, and 'penning' encloses the lines in it. Mary Wollstonecraft wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792).
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Wollstonecraft was an eighteenth-century English author and early champion of women's rights.

clue.text: When storm envelops pharisaical pretender

indicators.note: envelops means wraps around, so the first pieces surround the next

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to storm is to rage or rant
pi is slang for sanctimonious or pious, as a pharisee is

explanation.surface: A tempest wraps around a self-righteous imposter.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is the crossword sense of 'pharisaical' (self-righteous).
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone with ambitions to a position, as a pretender lays claim to a throne.

clue.text: Put part of spreadsheet in sequence without time for trial?

indicators.note: without means leaving out, so the abbreviation for time is dropped
in tells us the spreadsheet piece goes inside the word for sequence

parts.note: to sequence things is to sort them into order
a row is a horizontal line of cells in a spreadsheet

explanation.surface: An office worker orders a spreadsheet row with no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes SORROWT; 'without' then drops the time letter. 'trial' means hardship, not a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial in the sense of a painful affliction or tribulation is a cause of grief.

clue.text: Suppose Nestor's filling space in tabloid's margins

indicators.note: in places the filled space between the outer letters of the newspaper word
margins are the edges, so only the first and last letters of tabloid are used
filling means going inside, so the setter's word sits within the space

parts.note: an area is a space
Nestor, the setter, is also the genus of New Zealand parrots including the kea, so Nestor's gives kea's

explanation.surface: The setter's piece fills a gap in a popular paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestor is the setter's pseudonym and also the genus of the kea, a New Zealand parrot, so 'Nestor's' is KEA'S; 'margins' supplies T and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something as read is to assume it without needing it stated.

clue.text: Quite hostile to prosecutor, wins in the end — almost

indicators.note: in puts the prosecutor and wins inside the shortened word for the end
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: death is the end
DA is District Attorney, a US prosecutor
to gain is to win, so wins gives gains

explanation.surface: A hostile prosecutor nearly triumphs at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter to give DEAT; 'in' signals the container. DA (District Attorney) is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead against something means being firmly opposed to it.

clue.text: Bulging in the middle after festivity

indicators.note: in the middle picks out the central letter of the word bulging

parts.note: a la, French, means in the style of, or after

explanation.surface: Someone feels bloated around the waist after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a link word but gives A LA, as in 'after the manner of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special entertainment.

clue.text: Tot sum, forced to a limit?

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters are pushed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A child's arithmetic is pushed to the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's utmost means reaching the greatest extent possible, the furthest point.

clue.text: Confound it, CID cop's blind spot

indicators.note: confound means throw into confusion, so the following letters are mixed up

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and its S is used

explanation.surface: An exasperated officer curses a detective's oversight.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic disc is where the optic nerve leaves the eye; having no light receptors, it forms the eye's natural gap in vision.

clue.text: Randomly decide to make many sketches

definitions.meaning: to settle a matter by chance, picking straws or tickets
draw is sketch, and lots is many

explanation.surface: An artist leaves it to chance whether to produce a pile of drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing by lottery settles things by chance, while drawing plenty is producing a great number of pictures.

clue.text: Fix back on catamaran, turning in slight wind after front's come off

indicators.note: in puts the turned boat inside the trimmed wind word
the front letter of the wind word is removed

parts.note: a breath of wind is a slight breeze

indicators.note: turning means the boat word is read backwards

parts.note: a catamaran is a type of boat, a cat for short

explanation.surface: Someone repairs part of a catamaran that turned in a gentle breeze after the bow broke away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after front's come off' gives REATH; 'turning' reverses the boat to TAC, which goes 'in' just before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something back on is to attach it again after removal.

clue.text: Impetuous person has teaspoonful swallowed in time

indicators.note: swallowed in means taken inside, so the measure goes into the time word

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
tsp is the standard abbreviation for teaspoon or teaspoonful

explanation.surface: A rash person gulps down a spoonful of medicine on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotspur, Harry Percy in Shakespeare's Henry IV, gave his nickname to any rash, headstrong person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a hot-headed, rash individual, after Shakespeare's Harry Percy.

clue.text: Complete document that authorises leaving wife

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the abbreviation for wife is removed

parts.note: a warrant is a document giving authority, for example to search or arrest

explanation.surface: A divorce paper is finished once the wife walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means utter or out-and-out, as in 'arrant nonsense'.

clue.text: Boy's fastening cord, twisted at each end

definitions.note: the clue reads boy is; the definition is the boy

indicators.note: the two letters at the start are swapped, and so are the two at the finish

parts.note: a lace is a cord that fastens a shoe

explanation.surface: A boy's shoelace is twisted at both tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted at each end' swaps LA to AL and CE to EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a familiar male given name, short for Alexander.

clue.text: Preparation for an Italian place, bronze, getting away with 50% loss

parts.note: to place is to put
bronze is a colour, a suntan or tan

indicators.note: 50% loss means half the word goes, keeping its first four of eight letters

parts.note: getting away means escaping

explanation.surface: A tanned holidaymaker leaves a place having lost half their luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 50% loss' halves ESCAPING to ESCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Puttanesca is a spicy Italian pasta sauce with olives, capers and anchovies.

clue.text: Perhaps a Barrymore article in its Spanish translation

indicators.note: in puts the English article inside its Spanish counterpart

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An article about a famous actor appears in Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to 'article': the Spanish for THE is EL, which holds THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel Barrymore was an American stage and film actress, one of the Barrymore acting dynasty.

clue.text: Recall Scene One lines and start to learn words to perform

indicators.note: recall means call back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for scene in a play script
I is the Roman numeral for one
RY is short for railway, a crossword sense of lines

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of learn

explanation.surface: An actor goes over the first scene's lines before rehearsals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' reverses SC + I + RY + L as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrics are the words of a song, sung in performance.

clue.text: Star nearly collapsed

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: sunk means caved in or collapsed

explanation.surface: A celebrity almost faints.
explanation.definitionFit: Our own sun is a star at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: Someone continually attacked hard with cup-bang out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the letters are not in their proper arrangement

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A victim is assaulted repeatedly with a clattering cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges H with CUPBANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A punchbag is figuratively a person who suffers constant criticism or abuse.

clue.text: Harrowing Angelou tract leads to compliment

indicators.note: harrowing means breaking up the soil, so the letters are broken and remixed

explanation.surface: A distressing piece by Maya Angelou earns praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Maya Angelou was an American poet and memoirist.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate is to praise or pay tribute to someone on an achievement.
